items.text: Understand what the CLI is and why it's used over GUI for servers
Read and decode the terminal prompt (username, hostname, directory, $ vs #)
Know the Linux filesystem hierarchy starting from root (/)
Understand absolute vs relative paths and when to use each
Know what hidden files are and how to identify them (dot prefix)
Use pwd to confirm your current location at any time
Navigate directories using cd, cd .., cd ~, and multi-level paths
List files with ls, ls -a, ls -l, and ls -la — and know when to use each
Read ls -l output to identify file type, permissions, size, and owner
Create single and nested directories using mkdir and mkdir -p
Delete empty directories with rmdir and non-empty ones with rm -r
Delete files permanently using rm and understand the risks
Use cat to read file contents without opening an editor
Use history to review past commands and re-run them with !N
Clear the screen with clear or Ctrl+L
State what pwd, ls -a, ls -l, mkdir -p, rmdir, rm, cat, clear, and history each do
Explain the difference between $ (regular user) and # (root) in the prompt
Explain what happens if you lose your EC2 private key pair
Know that rmdir only works on empty directories and rm -r handles non-empty ones
Know that rm deletes permanently — no recycle bin in Linux CLI
